name: Restoration of Mongolian Citizenship (Former Citizens, Article 14)

qualifying_event.description: A person who lost Mongolian citizenship in specific circumstances may apply to the President (via the central state administrative body) to restore it: (a) citizenship lost due to a change in adoption status; (b) within 5 years of turning 18, if citizenship was lost as a minor due to a parent's change of citizenship; (c) a person who was a Mongolian citizen as of 11 July 1921 (Mongolia's revolution/independence date) and who subsequently acquired foreign citizenship; or (d) a person who renounced Mongolian citizenship intending to acquire a foreign one, but was ultimately unable to acquire that foreign citizenship (Law on Citizenship 1995, Article 14).
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Historical citizenship/civil-status documentation establishing the applicant's own prior Mongolian citizenship and the specific ground for loss.

requirement_groups.name: Standard route (any of Article 14's four grounds)

requirements.blocker_text: Meets one of Article 14's specific restoration grounds: loss via adoption change, loss as a minor via parental citizenship change (must apply within 5 years of turning 18), former citizenship as of 11 July 1921 followed by acquiring foreign citizenship, or renunciation followed by failure to acquire the intended foreign citizenship.

evidence_required.document: Historical proof of the applicant's own prior Mongolian citizenship
Documentation of the specific circumstances of loss

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: no ongoing residence in Mongolia is stated as a precondition to apply

sources.title: ecoi.net (Austrian Red Cross/ACCORD country-of-origin information network) -- Law of Mongolia on Citizenship, 5 June 1995, English translation, Article 14: restoration of citizenship for former citizens (adoption-change loss, minor parental-change loss within 5 years of majority, former citizens as of 11 July 1921 who acquired foreign citizenship, and those unable to acquire an intended foreign citizenship); applications go to the President via the central administrative body

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Mongolia). STATUS: DRAFT -- tier-2 only, same sourcing constraint as this build's other citizenship files. MODELING CAUTION, READ CAREFULLY: this file is deliberately scoped to EXACTLY what Article 14's text supports -- restoration for a person who WAS THEMSELVES a Mongolian citizen (as of 11 July 1921 or otherwise) and subsequently lost that status. It is NOT modeled as an open-ended multi-generation descent/diaspora route (unlike Romania's Article 11, which explicitly extends to descendants to the third degree) -- the fetched Article 14 text does not state a descendant provision, and none is assumed here. 11 July 1921 is Mongolia's national revolution/independence-proclamation date; the practical scope of this specific historical clause (how many people it could plausibly still apply to, a century later, absent a stated descendant extension) is genuinely unclear from the text alone and flagged for verification against a fuller/more current version of the law -- the ecoi.net copy's own filename references a 2009-2010-era timestamp, and this dataset could not confirm whether Article 14 has been amended since. This route requires no ongoing Mongolian residence to apply, a structural similarity to Romania's reacquisition route despite the narrower stated scope.
